title: Getting Around
description: Tell a taxi driver where to go, understand 'straight, right at the roundabout, stop here', and take a bus or the metro — with the commands you give from the back seat and the small etiquette of fixing the fare first.
approach: GPA Phase 2 — direction-giving from in-car footage. Commands are heard with the turn on screen, then drilled as a route on a map, then given aloud to a virtual driver.
unlock_condition: ≥12/16 on the follow-the-directions map quiz and a recorded route of four commands
can_do: Take a taxi or bus and say where you want to go
Say near, far, right, left, straight

grammar.title: Commands for the road: go, turn, stop
grammar.explanation: Directions are commands, and Gulf commands are short: روح 'go', لف 'turn', وقّف 'stop', كمّل 'keep going', ارجع 'go back'. Add the direction straight after: لف يمين, روح سيدة. To a woman driver add ـي (لفي، وقفي) and to more than one person ـوا (لفوا، وقفوا). To say 'don't', put لا in front of the present form: لا تلف هني 'don't turn here', لا توقف 'don't stop'. Soften any command with لو سمحت or الله يخليك — a Gulf passenger gives orders politely but gives them. The formal اذهب, انعطف and توقف are never said.

examples.english: Turn right at the traffic light
Go back a bit (to a woman)

culture.title: Fix the fare, then get in
culture.note: Everyone in the Gulf drives, so a taxi is for visitors, airports and nights out — and the apps (Careem, Uber) have replaced most street taxis, with the driver called الكابتن. In a street taxi with no meter, agree the price through the window before you sit: بكم للمطار؟ then خلاص، عشرين. Men sit in the front or the back; women sit in the back. Big cities have buses and Dubai and Riyadh have a metro, with women-and-family carriages at one end. Directions are given by landmark, not street name: 'after the mosque, at the second roundabout, next to the pharmacy'. Learn the landmarks and you will never need an address.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The English word, written تكسي or تاكسي. Saudis also say ليموزين for the old airport cabs. An app ride is كريم or أوبر and its driver الكابتن.
vocabulary.image_scene: A yellow-and-white taxi waiting at a kerb with its roof sign lit.

example.english: I want a taxi to the airport

vocabulary.video_hint: Hailing or ordering a taxi in a travel vlog; تكسي or كريم said.

vocabulary.teaching_note: English 'bus' with a long aa and an emphatic ص at the end: baaṣ. The formal حافلة is on signs only. The stop is موقف الباص.
vocabulary.image_scene: A large city bus pulling up to a shaded bus stop, passengers waiting.

example.english: The bus comes every half hour

vocabulary.video_hint: A bus or bus stop in a city vlog; الباص named as it arrives.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Long ii. Pairs with لف: لف يمين 'turn right'. On its own with a hand gesture it is a full instruction in a taxi. Same in every dialect.
vocabulary.image_scene: A large arrow curving to the right on a road sign.
vocabulary.video_hint: A passenger pointing right — يمين — from inside a car.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The standard word; many Gulf speakers also say شمال ('north') for left, so accept both. Long aa at the end.
vocabulary.image_scene: A large arrow curving to the left on a road sign.

example.english: The restaurant is on the left

vocabulary.video_hint: A direction given — يسار / شمال — with the turn visible.

vocabulary.teaching_note: A Gulf marker: siida 'straight'. Also على طول and, from older Kuwaitis, دغري. Combine with the go-verb: روح سيدة, or say it alone with a chopping hand forward.
vocabulary.image_scene: A straight empty highway running to the horizon between sand and palms.

example.english: Go straight until the traffic light

vocabulary.video_hint: A driver told سيدة / على طول with the road ahead on screen.

vocabulary.teaching_note: وقّف 'stop' (ق as g, doubled g) + هنا 'here' — Kuwaitis and Emiratis say هني. The phrase that ends every taxi ride. Also heard as the shorter وقف or the noun موقف for a stopping place.
vocabulary.image_scene: A passenger's hand signalling stop, a taxi pulling in beside a shop.

example.arabic: وقّف هنا لو سمحت، جنب الصيدلية
example.transliteration: waggif hina law samaḥt, jamb iṣ-ṣaydaliyya
example.english: Stop here please, next to the pharmacy

vocabulary.video_hint: The end of a ride — وقف هنا — as the car pulls over.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Long ii, with ع before it. بعيد؟ is the first thing to ask about any destination; the answer 'not far' is مو بعيد. Feminine بعيدة.
vocabulary.image_scene: A tiny building far away on the horizon at the end of a long road.

example.english: Is the airport far? — No, not far

vocabulary.video_hint: Someone asking or saying a place is بعيد in a travel vlog.

vocabulary.teaching_note: ق as g: gariib. قريب من 'near to'. Also 'relative' (a family member) and 'soon' — context decides. Feminine قريبة.
vocabulary.image_scene: Two buildings side by side with a short arrow between them.
vocabulary.video_hint: Someone reassuring قريب / قريب من هنا about a walk or a drive.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Doubled emphatic ṭ. Any station — metro, bus, train — and also the petrol station: محطة بنزين. Plural محطات.
vocabulary.image_scene: A modern metro station entrance with an escalator going down.
vocabulary.video_hint: A metro or bus station in a Dubai or Riyadh vlog; المحطة named.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Emphatic ط, long aa. The destination every visitor needs first: للمطار 'to the airport'. Plural مطارات.
vocabulary.image_scene: An airport terminal from outside, a plane taking off behind it.

example.english: The airport is far from the city

vocabulary.video_hint: An airport arrival or departure vlog; المطار in the opening.

vocabulary.teaching_note: The standard word, but in speech Gulf people very often say تكت (from 'ticket'). A metro card is بطاقة or نول in Dubai. Plural تذاكر.
vocabulary.image_scene: A metro ticket being tapped on a gate reader.

example.english: I want a ticket to Riyadh

vocabulary.video_hint: A ticket bought or checked at a station or airport; تذكرة or تكت said.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Doubled f, said sharp: liff. Always followed by the direction: لف يمين، لف يسار. As a full turn-around it is لف وارجع. Feminine لفي.
vocabulary.image_scene: A car mid-turn at a junction, its indicator on.

example.english: Turn left at the second roundabout

vocabulary.video_hint: A navigator saying لف with the car turning.

vocabulary.teaching_note: From ساق 'drive': doubled w, ق as g. The neutral word for any driver; an app driver is called الكابتن to his face. Feminine سواقة.
vocabulary.image_scene: A driver seen from the back seat, hands on the wheel, rear-view mirror visible.
vocabulary.video_hint: A taxi ride filmed from inside; the passenger addressing السواق / الكابتن.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Emphatic ط, ق as g: ṭariig. Both the road and 'the way': على الطريق 'on the way'. A neighbourhood street is شارع; a highway is طريق سريع. Plural طرق.
vocabulary.image_scene: A wide desert highway with a green road sign in Arabic and English.

example.english: The road to the sea is straight on

vocabulary.video_hint: Driving footage with الطريق named — a road trip vlog.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Gulf cities run on roundabouts, so directions count them: الدوار الأول، الدوار الثاني. Doubled w, long aa. The formal ميدان is not used for this.
vocabulary.image_scene: A large landscaped roundabout with a sculpture in the middle and cars circling.
vocabulary.video_hint: A roundabout approached in dashcam-style footage; الدوار in the directions.

vocabulary.teaching_note: Literally 'signal'. عند الإشارة 'at the lights' is the other great landmark. Plural إشارات. Kuwaitis also say سكنال.
vocabulary.image_scene: A traffic light on red over a busy junction, cars waiting.

example.english: Stop at the lights, then straight on

vocabulary.video_hint: Waiting at a red light in a driving vlog; الإشارة mentioned.

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.english: Peace be upon you. How much to Mubarakiya souq?

dialogue.speaker: Driver
dialogue.english: And upon you peace. Three dinars

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.arabic: روح سيدة، وعند الدوار لف يمين
dialogue.transliteration: ruuḥ siida, w-ʿind id-duwwaar liff yimiin
dialogue.english: Go straight, and at the roundabout turn right

dialogue.speaker: Passenger
dialogue.arabic: إي. وقّف هني لو سمحت، جنب الدكان
dialogue.transliteration: ii. waggif hini law samaḥt, jamb id-dukkaan
dialogue.english: Yes. Stop here please, next to the shop

sound_spotlight.explanation: Gulf commands are one syllable or two, with no extra vowel at the front: ruuḥ not uruuḥ, liff not ilfif. Say them clipped, like an English 'go!' or 'stop!'.

sound_spotlight.sound: ق = g in the road words
sound_spotlight.explanation: Three road words, three hard g's. The formal q would sound out of place in a taxi; keep it g.
'Until' in the Gulf is layn, not the formal حتى. It links a command to a landmark: go straight until the lights.

lesson_sequence.detail: A 60-second in-car clip: a passenger giving directions, the turns visible through the windscreen, no captions. The learner just follows the car.
Sixteen cards with illustration and audio; direction words play with an arrow animation, commands with the car moving.
Grammar card: روح / لف / وقّف with the feminine and plural forms and the لا negative; then a tap exercise choosing the right form for a pictured driver.
Map quiz: hear four commands in a row (سيدة، لف يسار، بعد الدوار، وقف هنا) and drag the car to where it ends up. Twelve routes.
Role-play: the app shows a map with a destination; the learner records the fare question and four commands to get there. The driver 'obeys' on screen.
Score screen; the learner's route plays back. Nudge: narrate your next journey in Gulf commands.

real_world_prompts.prompt: On your next journey, say each turn in your head as it happens: سيدة… لف يمين… وقف هنا.
real_world_prompts.context: Shown on the lesson-complete screen. Rehearses the commands on real movement.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Ask someone how to get somewhere with شلون أروح… ؟ and listen for landmarks — the roundabout, the mosque, the lights — rather than street names.
real_world_prompts.context: Next-day nudge. Activates the question from Lesson 2 and the landmark habit from the culture note.

real_world_prompts.prompt: Watch a Gulf taxi or driving vlog and count the roundabouts named. Directions here are counted in دوار.
real_world_prompts.context: Homework card. Passive recognition of the landmark vocabulary.

video_needs.scene: A taxi ride filmed from inside with the fare agreed and directions given; a metro or bus journey; a driving vlog naming roundabouts and lights as they pass.
